title: Selected bit profile alone exceeds the κ=0.1 moment budget
body:
## Result

This follow-up to [PR #3107](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3107) certifies an exact local-only lower bound for the selected bit supplier at the requested target `κ = 0.1` (`a = 1/9` under the retained conversion).

The pinned local histogram `{1:1323, 2:1342, 3:79, 4:44, 5:102, 6:11, 7:19}`, normalized by `w = 296/3`, has outward-rational moment `1.195679601525` by itself. This deletes the centre charge and every idle child. Therefore, any change that keeps this histogram and call width cannot pass by changing unpaid-coordinate coverage alone: the local terms already exceed one.

For comparison, under the hypothetical `u=2`, `R=53` law, the full relaxed profile costs `1.355508` centre-free and `1.365696` with the centre. The ideal aggregate floor of `0.999452` does not describe the selected word. Uniform fractional repacking of the same rank mass first passes at rank 48 centre-free or rank 53 with the centre; this is a profile sensitivity only, not a realizable supplier.

This result is scoped to the selected word and call width. A different local word or changed `w` remains open. It constructs no endpoint and claims no κ improvement; the selected κ remains `0.001672660197076918`.

## Validation

- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/kappa010-rank-cap-floor` passed.
- `python3.12 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/kappa010-rank-cap-floor` and the corresponding complex-package byte check passed at head `fcba8eab38c51f4cdb685559be505222d44f8ddc`.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed; the PR contains only the five-file package delta.

Exact intervals, source pins, limitations and next questions are in [the rank-cap package](research/kappa010-rank-cap-floor/README.md). Canonical main was refreshed to `997e6a9ca7b4f95d50e366f61412fd640d72a88a` (priority revision 6); the selected result and pinned quantitative inputs are unchanged.

Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; predecessor attribution is recorded in the package.
